raster.not_tiff: This is not a TIFF file BimCraft can read ({reason}).
raster.bad_size: The image size in this file ({w} × {h}) is not usable.
raster.bad_cells: The cell values in this file ({bits}-bit, format {fmt}) are not a kind BimCraft reads.

raster.bands_n.one: The file has {n} band; the first is read as elevations.
raster.bands_n.other: The file has {n} bands; the first is read as elevations.

raster.no_georef: The file has no georeferencing (no tie point and pixel size), so BimCraft cannot place it.
raster.zero_cell: The file’s cell size is zero.
raster.unknown_unit: The file names its elevation unit as “{unit}”, which BimCraft does not know: say what it is.
raster.asc.not_asc: This is not an ASCII grid BimCraft can read (ncols/nrows missing or out of range).
raster.asc.no_cell: The ASCII grid has no usable cell size.
raster.asc.no_corner: The ASCII grid has no lower-left corner.
raster.asc.no_prj: The grid does not say which coordinate system it is in (no .prj file).
raster.asc.prj_big: The .prj file is too large to be a coordinate system description.
raster.no_grid: No elevation grid (.tif, .tiff or .asc) among the files.
raster.no_overlap: The area does not overlap the grid.
raster.area_big: The area covers {cells} cells; BimCraft reads at most {max} at once. Pick a smaller area.
raster.read_failed: The grid could not be read: the file may be cut short or damaged ({reason}).
raster.asc.short: The ASCII grid is shorter than its header says ({read} of {total} values).
raster.image_reduced: The image is {w} × {h} pixels; it was read at {rw} × {rh}.
render.title: Render a picture
render.sun.site: Sun on {date} at {time}, at the site's latitude ({lat}°).
render.sun.assumed: Sun on {date} at {time}, at 40° north: the file does not say where the site is.
render.sun.own: Use another date and time for this picture
render.sun.down: It is night at that time: the sky is dark, so the model's lamps light it.
render.looks.hint: How each color looks. Glass lets the sky show through. Light bending through glass and mirrors reflecting the model need the high-quality mode.
render.nogl: This browser can't render pictures: it has no WebGL 2.
render.stopped: Stopped after {passes} passes ({s} s). Save PNG keeps this picture.
render.empty: Nothing to render: nothing is shown.

render.mode.fast.note: Daylight, soft shadows and the sky’s reflections, in seconds.
render.mode.hq.note: Light bouncing between surfaces, real glass and mirrors. Much slower: start small, and give it a time limit.
render.hq.stopped: Stopped after {passes} samples ({s} s). Save PNG keeps this picture.
render.budget: Stopped at the time limit after {passes} samples ({s} s). Save PNG keeps this picture.
render.hq.load: The high-quality mode could not load: {error}
res.tools.title: More building tools: roof planes and the rest of the residential set
res.rf.plate.auto: blank = the top of the walls
res.err.nopitch: At least one wall under a roof has to be pitched.
res.err.overhang: The overhangs are too deep for this outline: the eave would cross itself.
res.err.shape: This outline is too small or folded to put a roof on.
res.tool.roofplane.title: Draw one roof plane by its corners: the first side is the eave
res.hint.roofplane: Click the corners: the first side is the eave. Click the first corner again or press Enter to finish.
res.err.plane: A roof plane needs at least three corners around some area.
res.tool.foundation.title: Put a foundation under the walls: slab, stem walls, crawlspace or basement
res.hint.foundation: Point inside the building and click: the foundation follows the outside of its walls.
res.fd.autonote: Sizes marked auto are labelled defaults from the walls and the number of stories ({n}), not engineering: a designer or engineer checks them for the soil and the loads. Type 0 to go back to auto.
res.fd.picked: This building has a foundation: change it in Properties.
res.err.fdkind: That kind of foundation is not one BimCraft makes.
res.err.fdsize: These sizes leave nothing to build: make the walls or the footing narrower than the building.
res.tool.countertop.title: Put a countertop on a run of base cabinets from the library
res.hint.countertop: Point at a run of base cabinets and click: one countertop over all of them. Click a run that has one to fit it again.
res.ct.gone: No cabinets under it any more.
res.ct.hud.fit: {n} cabinets, {area}: click to fit its countertop again
res.err.nocabinet: Point at base cabinets from the library (the residential set): a countertop goes on them.
res.tool.stair.title: Draw a stair: straight, L, U or with winders, sized from the floor-to-floor height
res.hint.stair: Click where the stair starts (the middle of the bottom step), then click the way up.
res.tool.railing.title: Draw a railing with balusters: a deck edge, a balcony, round an opening in a floor
res.hint.railing: Click along the railing; double-click or press Enter to finish.
res.st.checks.ok: Meets the labelled defaults (riser at most 7¾", tread at least 10", 36" wide, handrail 34"–38"). They are not engineering: the building official decides.
res.st.checks.bad: Outside the labelled defaults: {list}. They are not engineering: the building official decides.
res.err.rail: A railing needs at least two points.
res.err.stairkind: That kind of stair is not one BimCraft makes.
res.err.stairwidth: A stair is between 500 mm and 5 m wide.
res.err.stairshort: Too few steps for a turn: make it straight, or the floors farther apart.
res.tool.framing.title: Frame walls, floors and roofs: studs, joists, rafters or trusses, kept with the model
res.hint.framing: Click a wall, a floor or a roof on its level to frame it; or frame every wall at once.
res.fr.keep: Keep this piece when the framing is made again
res.fr.kept: Kept: it stays when the framing is made again
res.fr.check: The framing round it changed: check where it is.
res.fr.note: Sizes come from labelled default tables (headers by opening width, joists, rafters and ceiling joists by span), not engineering: a designer or engineer checks spans and loads.
res.fr.note.header: An opening is wider than the header table: a designer sizes that header (an engineered beam is usual).
res.fr.note.headerroom: A header doesn't fit under the plates: the opening is too tall for this wall.
res.fr.note.joist: The span is longer than the joist table: a designer sizes these joists (engineered joists are usual).
res.fr.note.rafter: The rafters run farther than the rafter table: a designer sizes them.
res.fr.note.ceiling: The ceiling joists span farther than their table: a designer sizes them.
res.err.noframe: Point at a drawn wall with studs, a floor or a roof to frame it.
res.err.nostuds: This wall type has no studs to frame (block, concrete).
res.err.shortwall: This wall is too short to frame.
res.tool.terrain.title: The site's ground: from survey points, contours, a LAS / LAZ scan, a GeoTIFF, or spot elevations
res.hint.terrain: Open a survey file, or type an elevation (from this level's floor) and click spots on the plan, then Make the ground.
res.tool.pad.title: Cut a flat pad for the house into the ground, with slopes out to the existing grade
res.hint.pad: Point inside a building and click: its pad goes under it with the margin and slopes set here.
res.tool.paving.title: A driveway, walk or patio draped on the ground
res.hint.paving: Click the corners; click the first corner again, double-click or press Enter to finish.
res.tr.xml.title: Download the existing and finished ground as LandXML: open it in CivilCraft for real grading
res.tr.xmldone: Downloaded the ground as LandXML: open it in CivilCraft.
res.tr.raise.note: (moves the survey up; a negative value lowers it)
res.tr.hud.spot: Click a spot at {z} ({n} so far)
res.err.spots: Click at least three spots first.
res.err.nosurvey: No points with elevations in that file.
res.err.surface: Could not make a surface from those points (are they all in a line?).
res.err.terrainthere: The model has its ground already: delete it to start again.
res.err.nosite: The model has no site to put the ground in.
res.err.ifc4: The ground needs an IFC4 model (this one is IFC2x3).
res.err.hardscape: Paving needs at least three corners.
res.err.hardscapeoff: That paving is off the ground.
res.err.tinload: The ground is still loading: try again in a moment.
res.tool.section.title: A section line: click its two ends; it looks to the left of the line
res.sec.name: Section {name}
res.sec.label: Label
res.sec.hud.a: Click where the section line starts
res.sec.hud.b: Click where it ends (it looks to the side the short line shows)
res.err.sectionshort: A section line needs two ends at least 100 mm apart.
res.sh.title: Sheets
res.sh.open.title: Sheets: plans, elevations, sections, schedules and framing, ready to print
res.sh.done: The drawing set is downloading ({n} sheets).
res.sh.making: Drawing the sheets from the model…
res.sh.none: Nothing to draw yet: draw some walls first.
res.sh.failed: The sheets could not be drawn: {why}
res.tool.electrical.title: Outlets, switches, lights and panels on the plan
res.hint.electrical: Choose a device, then click: outlets, switches and panels go on the nearest wall, lights on the ceiling.
res.hint.ellink: Click the lights this switch turns on (click one again to unlink it). Enter or Esc when done.
res.el.link.status: Click the lights {tag} switches; Enter when done.
res.el.link.row: Click lights to link them to the switch, or click a linked one to unlink it.
res.err.elwall: Outlets, switches and panels go on a wall: click near one.
res.err.elnotswitch: Only switches and sensors turn lights on.
res.to.title: The model's quantities to TakeoffCraft: a plan of each level with the takeoff inside, the trade packs' assemblies on the items
res.to.cutnote: Each dot is one piece, counted by TakeoffCraft. Lengths are the stock to order.
res.to.none: Nothing to take off yet: draw some walls first.
res.to.sent: Sent to TakeoffCraft: {items} items, {marks} marks. Open the takeoff it found in the PDF there.
res.to.saved: Downloaded {file}: open it in TakeoffCraft, which finds the takeoff inside.
res.to.failed: The takeoff could not be made: {why}
input.style.viewer.hint: For opening and checking models: File, View, Show, Check and Edit menus and a row of viewing tools (fit, top, front, side, section, measure, hide, isolate, see-through, walk). The drawing tools wait in the Model menu at the end.
